provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Find the smallest periodic full-line partition with a non-background divider colour shared by both axes. Crop the unique panel containing background and exactly one other colour. Operate directly in visible coordinates; palette[0] is the only specialized colour. No fallback geometry or panel ranking.
draft_notes.limitations: Certified for unchanged native random domain and supplied fixtures. Arbitrary explicit colors outside that domain may lack a unique qualifying panel and are rejected. The native random domain has exactly one {0,F} panel, every other panel contains 0 plus at least two nonzero colours, D and F are nonzero and different.

host_review.reason: Any candidate divider period q <= true panel width s has a candidate cut inside the unique target panel. Such a full cut crosses real perpendicular dividers, so its colour would have to be D. Inside the target it meets only 0 or F, neither D. Contradiction. Thus no smaller period passes; the true one does. The claim uses the target panel as an input witness, not its stored output. The same reasoning holds after any D4 transform and bijective palette.
host_review.random_color_verified: common.random_color selects from 1..9; fg excludes divider.
host_review.source_changes: Removed arbitrary uniform-line fallback and fewer-colour/count/reading-order ranking. Require unique background-plus-one-colour panel.
host_review.verification: Fresh 1000 unique inputs,8000 augmented pair checks,16 fixtures passed. Three adversarial tests pass: all222native geometry/target placements, all385smaller-period/target cases, each16D4/palette variants; ambiguous/missing structures rejected.
